reading.ours: two units of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — an instrument check, and it is printed first because nothing below it means anything until it passes. The true ratio is a little UNDER 2: both sides pay the driving loop once, so the exact expectation is (2u + L) / (u + L) with L the loop and u one unit, which at sixteen dependent steps per unit puts it around 1.9. A reading below 1.5 means this process could not resolve a deliberate doubling, and the runner voids the report rather than printing prices under it.

reading.ours: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: the same body again, over its own copy of the same state
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — the noise floor. The two sides are identical code over identical, separately-allocated state, so the true ratio is 1.00 exactly and every departure from it printed here was produced by this machine at this moment. The rule that follows is the one the whole table is read under: NO RATIO CLOSER TO 1.00 THAN THIS GAP IS A READING. It also bounds the per-row noise figure, which is the same idea measured again inside every pair — each pair times its floor twice, once before our side and once after, and prints how far the two disagreed.

reading.ours: one updateEntityColumn on a held root, no effect, no flush
reading.floor: one root(v) with no batch; one alien effect on the root runs after the write
reading.caveat: ONE OPERATION IS ONE WRITE TO ONE ROOT, and ours stops at: the write. ARCHITECTURAL POINT: none; this row splits graph.coalescing.unbatched.k1, whose ours side is one write, one channel.flush() and one effect run. Every row of this group stands against the same floor, one alien write with one alien effect on the root, so the ns difference between two rows of the group is the price of the step one row adds over the other. The write-and-effect-run row calls effectService.runEffectIfSourcesChanged directly, so it pays the effect service and no frame; after its first write the frame never closes, so the slot counts as changed in the open frame and the write enlists nothing more. Ours is @oimdb/core from source: an OIMSingleEntity root written through entityContentService.updateEntityColumn, OIMSingleComputed nodes for anything derived, one effect from OIMEffectService, and channel.flush() as the settle. The floor is alien-signals 3.2: signal, computed, effect, and startBatch/endBatch where the row says so. Every write stores a new number from a counter, so no write on either arm is stopped by a same-value check. Each arm runs in its own process.
